summary: Five critics went through Set up my plan as a newcomer, a money checker, an engineer, a designer and an accessibility tester; all 51 problems they confirmed are fixed.
points: Nothing typed is lost: the phone keyboard's Next moves to the next box instead of skipping the question, and Back keeps what you typed.
Change an answer lists the seven questions with your answers and brings you straight back to where you stand.

The numbers are right in more cases: a blank payment gets a typical one (marked), a mortgage asks what the home is worth, and accounts or cards added later on their own pages no longer make the setup drop its own.
The end screen tells the truth: its sentence matches the figures, a retiree living on savings is told so calmly, the first moves are in plain words, and nothing glows green when nothing was entered.
Choices work with the keyboard and screen readers: one Tab stop with arrow keys, help read out with each box, the question number in the heading.

shots.caption: The end screen: the sentence names the costly card first, the net worth says the home is not in yet, the moves are in plain words.
Change an answer: each question with what the plan holds; a tap opens it and Save comes straight back.
Every question skipped: no green, no celebration, each figure links to the question that fills it.

summary: On a computer, the setup's four end figures sit two by two instead of four squeezed in a row.
points: Each figure keeps the large size on a wide screen.
